On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object

Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: every wrong submission costs 1 and every demo request costs 1. An
instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt cap is reached, and
reaching the cap is charged the full cap. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

## Noisy binary grid with a colored stencil (validated 2026-09-29)

A task had a random-looking grid of background values `0` and `4` (demo used `0` and `8`), plus a small object colored `5`. Other cells in each bounding box are irrelevant; existing nonzero noise is preserved; overlapping matches contribute the union of their stencil cells. This rule produced a submission confirmed CORRECT.

Procedure for similar instances: identify the special-color stencil offsets; scan every in-bounds translation against the original grid; accept a translation only if every stencil offset lands on `0`; recolor those matched cells to the special color and preserve all other cells. Do not mutate during match detection (or accidentally let prior marks create new matches).
